units.translation: 21 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Δίνδυμον: a mountain of Phrygia. I 985–986 (ἁλός). Apollonius. Aura was a certain maiden, beautiful, fond of hunting, living in Pontus. Once when she was hunting with Artemis, Dionysus saw her and forced her, making her pregnant. Artemis saw her and chased her with threats. Fearing the goddess's anger, Aura went from Pontus to Cyzicus and went up onto the mountain, where she gave birth to twins, on account of which they called the mountain Dindymon. Or because it has two peaks, it was called Dindymon.
to belong, as Philostephanus says (fr. 2 M. III 29), so named; and all Phrygia is sacred to the goddess. Or because it has two peaks it is so called.

4 Etymologicum Genuinum (B) Χυτῷ λιμένι: Chytos harbor of Cyzicus. Chytos is called the one enclosed and built with stones and not natural. It is also called that which has mud and silt, that is, filth. cf. W 82 on the whole passage see Tümpel Phil. 56, 1897, 340; Aem. Knorr De Ap. Rh. Arg. fontibus, Diss. Lips. 1902, 17; Knaack Herm. 37, 1902, 292
5 γὰρ instead of δὲ in F; Δηίοχος in LV : Διίοχος in P
9 ἐξήλασαν in AH : ἐξελα. (sic) in L : omitted in P
11 Δηίοχος in V : Διίοχος in P : Δηίλοχος in L

12 lacuna indicated by W. It seems to have been said according to Deiochus that the Pelasgians made an attack on the Argonauts as Thessalians : 〈διὰ τὸ〉 Θετταλοὺς εἶναι οὗτος δὲ Γ. φ. ἐγχ. W : φ. ἐγχ. τοὺς δὲ Γ. φ.

13 deleted by W on the advice of Ed. Schwartz De Dion. Scytobr., Diss. Bonn. 1880, 11 n. 1. After these words L repeats from scholium 987a ὡς Δηίοχος (Πολύγνωστος too audaciously Wachsmuth ap. Knorr l. l. 18). The words Πολύγνωστος — λέγει from scholium 996/97, where in L they are inserted after λέοντος, Ed. Fitch in a letter dated 15 October 1910 to Deicke transferred here with P. Perhaps the whole sentence should be restored thus: οὗτος — ἐπιβουλεῦσαι, Πολύγνωστος δὲ ἐν τοῖς Περὶ Κυζίκου δοκοῦντας λῃστὰς αὐτοὺς εἶναι 〈...〉.

17 added by W 39, since the meaning of the scholium seems to be this: Apollonius represented the Cyzicene monsters as having been reared by Juno to increase the glory of Hercules, just as commonly the Nemean lion, and according to Callimachus the Cerynean hind, are believed to have been.
that the Earthborn were reared for Heracles. The story is from the Nemean lion. Callimachus also mentions it where he says (Hymn III 107–09):
5 πάγος Κερύνειος ἔδεκτο in the manuscripts of Callimachus : πάγος Κεραύνιος ἔδεκτο in L : πάγης που δέκτο κεραυνοῦ in P
6 scholium 1081 with similar passages. 7 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) δῆθεν: I 998. δῆθεν is sometimes a filler word for δή, sometimes like δή.
8 σὺν in W : ὡς in L : lacking in P
10 ἢ ἀνεκπλήκτως added after ἀδ. in P
14 κατὰ πάντα in AH, cf. W 31
